column1: # PS-T3 micro-bench — broad per-keystroke prefix sweep (group<TAB>query)
# Purpose: measure latency at the SHORT-prefix end (the per-keystroke worst case
# that EXP-D2 left open). Groups are charset×length so `recall`/`pathquery`
# report p50/p95/p99 PER (charset, prefix-length). Members are deliberately the
# BROADEST substrings we expect in torrent paths (largest match-sets = slowest
# queries) — the bench is a worst-case probe, not a representative-query probe.
# Length is the # of chars a user has typed. min-chars=3 is the design floor, so
# ascii3/cjk3 are the GATE rows (G3 = broadest-3-char < 50 ms warm p50); the
# 2-char rows are included to quantify what min-chars=3 buys, and 4/5-char rows
# to show the selectivity gradient as the user keeps typing.
# ASCII members lean on release-name boilerplate (years, codecs, resolutions,
# scene tags) — the highest-frequency substrings in the corpus.
# --- 2 chars (broadest; below the min-chars=3 floor — diagnostic only) -------
# --- 3 chars (THE GATE: broadest realistic firing query) ---------------------
# --- CJK 2 chars (broadest CJK; below the floor — diagnostic) ----------------
